The urea cycle regenerates ornithine after it combines with carbamoyl phosphate to form citrulline, which is later converted back to ornithine after arginine is cleaved. This regeneration is analogous to how oxaloacetate in the citric acid cycle is regenerated at the end of the cycle after being converted through a series of intermediates.  

- (A) Succinate is an intermediate but not regenerated in the same way.  
- (B) Fumarate is produced but not the regenerated starting molecule.  
- (C) Oxaloacetate is the regenerated starting molecule of the citric acid cycle.  
- (D) Citrate is the first intermediate, not regenerated.  

Final answer: (C)
